major_findings.problem: I previously classified the pre-shuffle deterministic sort as dead code that obscures selection order. The coordinator's cross-examination directs me to use the supplied executable counterexample.
major_findings.concrete_evidence_or_counterexample: reports/revision_audit/sampling_sort_counterexample.json records 'production_sort_makes_input_order_irrelevant': true and 'removing_sort_changes_selection_under_reordered_input': true, with distinct source_id lists before and after removal. Python's Mersenne Twister shuffle output depends on list length and element positions; without the canonical sort, different caller input orders produce different internal list layouts, causing identical seeds to yield different selections. My prior claim was factually incorrect.
major_findings.repair_or_test: Retain the sort. Add an inline comment at line 38: '# Canonical sort ensures seed-deterministic selection regardless of caller input order.'
